Top-level asks (this week):

- Share any compatibility constraints for your vector store (namespace conventions, id formats, key rotation windows).
- Approve the proposed backfill window: Aug 30, 22:00–02:00 PT (4 hours, rolling shards).

What Redwood will do:
- Run a 5k sample ingest to our staging vectorstore and run rerank smoke tests (MRR, recall@10, latency p95).
- Provide a short runbook for the backfill (index ordering, chunking strategy, throttling knobs).
- Observe privacy/SOC2 notes and work with your security contact on access controls.

I've attached a short checklist and a sample prompts file to speed up validation.

If the August 30 window works, we will follow the runbook below and do a canary on 1% of traffic before full cutover.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Preflight: Embeddings cutover — sampling, DB sync, & rerank eval plan

Jared,

CSV with columns (id, text) + separate embeddings payload is fine — we can ingest either raw text and run Redwood embeddings or accept your exported float vectors. A couple of notes on the FAISS/quantization surface:

- Compatibility: FAISS indexes exported as raw float32 arrays are ideal. If certain shards are stored quantized (float16 or PQ), we will re-encode them during staging; please include a note per-shard in the manifest so we can avoid mismatches.
- Namespace/id mapping: we'll map tenant_{org_id} -> customer_namespace and keep your UUIDs as source_id. Confirm there are no duplicate ids across namespaces.
- Backfill strategy: incremental shard-based backfill with deterministic ordering. Plan:
  - Phase 1 (Canary): 5k sample ingest + rerank smoke (MRR, recall@10, avg latency token and p95 generation);
  - Phase 2 (Shard backfill): Backfill shards in batches of ~250k records with a 30-second throttle between batches to control IO;
  - Phase 3 (Cutover): Switch read routing to Redwood's vectorstore adapter with a 1% traffic canary for 45 minutes then 100% if stable.
- Downtime: we will aim for no user-visible downtime but recommend a short read-fallback policy for 10 minutes during the final routing switch.

Rerank eval criteria (what we'll measure during the smoke tests):
- MRR (top-10)
- Recall@10 and Recall@50
- Regression rate vs baseline (target <1.5% degradation on labeled eval set)
- End-to-end query p95 latency (target <250ms)
- Token-generation time per response for long-form rerank candidates

I'll attach the preliminary runbook and the small checklists. Karthik/Tessa — can you confirm whether we should reserve dedicated capacity for the backfill (GPU pool) or run on shared staging GPUs? Recommendation: reserve a small dedicate pool for QPS isolation.

Irene
